To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

regional headquarters are able to develop a high degree of strategic autonomy and to influence strategic decision making, but only if the regional headquarters is established as an independent entity, if the organizational structure is designed in such a way that it allows for strategic autonomy and the regional headquarters is located in a region that offers a high degree of autonomy.
regional headquarters of emerging markets multinations are in a distinct position between the mother company and subsidiaries.

regional units of emerging market multinational corporations are in a distinct position between headquarters and subsidiaries, and that their ability to act sustainably depends on their organizational set up, their regional embedding, and particularly on the respective regional managers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of regional headquarters as a specific organizational form in emerging market multinational corporations.
the question how the regional unit of emerging market multinationals can be empowered to contribute to a sustainable regional development.
the question how emerging market regional headquarters in Europe manage the tension between mother company and subsidiaries and what are the implications for regional autonomy and long term survival.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regional headquarters of emerging market multinationals are not just transmission mechanisms, but can have a significant impact on the organization.

regional headquarters in emerging markets multinationational corporations are not just transmission mechanisms, rather, depending on the respective context, they may have a high potential for autonomy and strategic influence.
regional units are neither mere implementers of a general plan, nor are they fully autonomous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
regional headquarters can act as strategic centers, but that this potential is not yet fully utilized.
regional units are in a constant process of negotiation between headquarters and subsidiaries, and that their autonomy is a result of this process.
regional units in emerging markets multinational corporations can be influential, but that their potential for autonomy depends on the distribution of power and control in the organization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regional units of emerging market multinationals have to deal with the same problems of organizational control and power games as their western counterparts.
regional units are in a position to develop and maintain a regional identity and to influence corporate strategy, if they are able to build up a power base and to act as a unit.
regional headquarters are not just passive transmission units, rather they can be powerful players, depending on their set up and the respective regional managers.
